question.text: Under the PMLA framework, KYC / client-identity and account-file records must be maintained for how long after the business relationship has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later?

answer.text: 3 years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed, whichever is later
7 years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed, whichever is later
10 years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed, whichever is later
5 years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed, whichever is later

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that KYC / client-identity and account-file records must be kept for five years after the business relationship has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later. The trigger that runs latest is the one used. The Trap: Stating the period only as "5 years after the business relationship ends" misses the "or account has been closed, whichever is later" leg — both events must be considered and the later one starts the clock. Note: The five-year retention runs from the later of business-relationship end and account closure; do not destroy records based on only one of those events.
